Name: Zhuu's II - Automated Farmhand
Author: yhh2324
Description:
[heading]Mechanical Farmhand[/heading]
[b]Mechanical Farmhand[/b] adds a fully functional agricultural robot to Stardew Valley.
Rather than simply placing an automation item in the crafting menu, the mod introduces the robot through existing parts of Stardew Valley: the Museum, Dwarven technology, Maru, and Clint.
As your collection grows and your relationships with the people involved improve, you will eventually take part in a small questline surrounding an experimental farming machine. Completing that story rewards you with your first Mechanical Farmhand and unlocks the recipe needed to build more of them.
The robot is designed as a later-game farming tool: powerful enough to reduce repetitive farm work, but still dependent on fuel, materials, storage, and preparation.
[line]
[heading]Dwarven Technology[/heading]
The first part of the progression begins at the Museum.
After donating all [b]four Dwarf Scrolls[/b] and [b]one Dwarf Gadget[/b], you will unlock a new recipe for producing the [b]Dwarf Gadget[/b].
This gives the otherwise rare Dwarven component a practical role in the construction of advanced farming technology.
The robot is therefore not something that appears at the beginning of a new save. Its technology is tied to exploration, artifact collection, and the gradual discovery of Stardew Valley's Dwarven machinery.
[line]
[heading]Unlocking the Mechanical Farmhand[/heading]
The main robot storyline becomes available once you have met all of the following conditions:
[b]30 minerals donated to the Museum, 4 hearts with Maru, and 4 hearts with Clint.[/b]
Once those conditions are met, the Mechanical Farmhand storyline can begin.
Maru and Clint are working on an experimental machine designed to assist with agricultural work, and the player becomes involved in completing the prototype.
Finishing the questline rewards you with:
[b]one completed Mechanical Farmhand and the crafting recipe needed to build additional robots.[/b]
This means your first robot is obtained through the story itself rather than immediately requiring you to craft one.
After that, you are free to expand the system and build additional Farmhands as your farm develops.
[line]
[heading]How the Robot Works[/heading]
The Mechanical Farmhand performs its work in the [b]early morning[/b].
At the beginning of its work cycle, each robot consumes:
[b]1 Coal[/b]
After receiving fuel, the robot begins processing the farmland within its assigned working area.
The robot can perform several basic farming jobs:
[list]
[*]harvesting crops;[/*]
[*]tilling soil;[/*]
[*]applying fertilizer;[/*]
[*]planting seeds;[/*]
[*]watering crops.[/*]
[/list]This allows a single Mechanical Farmhand to handle much of the repetitive work involved in maintaining a crop field.
The system is intentionally focused on ordinary agricultural work. It is not intended to completely replace the player or automate every system in Stardew Valley.
[line]
[heading]Working Range[/heading]
Each Mechanical Farmhand operates around its own [b]Robot Pod[/b].
The pod acts as the center of the robot's working area.
The Farmhand can work within a [b]25-tile range centered on the Robot Pod[/b].
Because the working area is tied to the pod, placement matters. You can position the pod beside the field you want the robot to maintain, and multiple robots can be used to cover different farming areas.
This keeps the automation physically connected to the farm itself rather than functioning as a global, invisible system.
[line]
[heading]Robot Pod[/heading]
Each Mechanical Farmhand uses a separate [b]Robot Pod[/b].
The Robot Pod is also a functional storage container.
You can open it like a normal storage chest and place items inside it, allowing the robot's supplies to remain close to the area where it works.
The pod therefore serves several purposes at once: it represents the robot's home base, defines the center of its working range, and provides local storage for the farming setup.
This makes the robot feel like an actual piece of farm equipment placed in the world instead of a background automation effect.
[line]
[heading]Fuel[/heading]
Every Mechanical Farmhand requires [b]1 Coal per work cycle[/b].
The coal is consumed in the early morning when the robot begins working.
This gives the robot a small but continuous operating cost.
Mechanical Farmhand intentionally uses a simple fuel system rather than batteries, rechargeable energy bars, or complicated power networks. Coal is easy to understand, already integrated into Stardew Valley's economy, and keeps the machine useful without making its automation completely free.
[line]
[heading]Automate Compatibility[/heading]
Mechanical Farmhand includes compatibility with [b]Automate[/b].
If Automate is installed, the Robot Pod can participate in compatible automation setups, allowing the Mechanical Farmhand to fit naturally into farms that already make extensive use of automated storage and processing.
Automate is [b]optional[/b].
You do not need Automate to use the robot, its storage pod, its farming functions, or its storyline.
Players who prefer a more traditional farm can use Mechanical Farmhand by itself, while players with larger automated setups can integrate it into their existing infrastructure.
[line]
[heading]Progression and Balance[/heading]
Mechanical Farmhand is deliberately placed later in progression.
Before gaining access to the robot, the player must explore, contribute to the Museum, discover Dwarven technology, and build relationships with Maru and Clint.
Even after unlocking it, the machine still requires fuel and thoughtful placement.
The goal is not to make farming irrelevant.
Instead, Mechanical Farmhand represents another stage in the development of an established farm: after upgrading tools, building sprinklers, constructing machines, and discovering more advanced technology, the player can finally begin delegating some of the routine field work to a mechanical assistant.
[line]
[heading]Design Philosophy[/heading]
Mechanical Farmhand was designed around a simple idea:
[b]automation should feel like part of Stardew Valley's world.[/b]
The robot does not simply appear as a menu option.
Its technology comes from Dwarven machinery.
Its development involves Maru and Clint.
Its components are tied to Museum progression.
Its operation requires fuel.
Its working range is physically centered around a machine placed on your farm.
The intention is for the Mechanical Farmhand to feel like something that was actually invented and built within Stardew Valley.
It is not just an invisible farming shortcut.
It is a machine that becomes part of your farm.
[line]
[heading]Requirements[/heading]
[b]Required:[/b] SMAPI
[b]Optional:[/b] Automate
Designed for [b]Stardew Valley 1.6[/b].
[line]

[heading]Mechanical Farmhand — 机械农场助手[/heading]
[b]Mechanical Farmhand[/b] 为《星露谷物语》增加了一台真正能够参与农业生产的机械农场助手。
这个模组并不是简单地把“自动种田”做成一个可以直接制作的机器，而是尽量让机器人的出现融入星露谷原本的世界。
它的技术来源与博物馆收集、矮人科技有关，而机器本身则通过马鲁与克林特共同参与的一段小型剧情逐渐完成。
随着玩家不断收集矿物和文物、提升与相关人物的关系，最终可以参与农业机器人原型机的开发。
完成相关剧情后，玩家会直接获得[b]第一台机械农场助手[/b]，同时解锁它的[b]制作配方[/b]，之后便可以根据自己的农场规模制造更多机器人。
[line]
[heading]矮人科技与前置解锁[/heading]
机械农场助手的技术线首先从博物馆开始。
当玩家向博物馆捐献：
[b]4份矮人卷轴 + 1个矮人小工具[/b]
之后，会解锁新的[b]矮人小工具制作配方[/b]。
这样，原本较为稀有的矮人小工具就不再只是一个偶然获得的古代物品，而会成为后续农业机械技术的重要组件。
这也意味着机械农场助手不会在新存档刚开始时就出现。
玩家需要先探索矿洞、收集文物、推进博物馆收藏，并逐渐接触到矮人科技，之后才有机会进入真正的机器人开发阶段。
[line]
[heading]如何解锁机械农场助手[/heading]
与机器人有关的主要剧情需要同时满足三个条件：
[b]博物馆捐献30种矿物。[/b]
[b]马鲁好感达到4心。[/b]
[b]克林特好感达到4心。[/b]
满足这些条件后，机械农场助手相关剧情便会开始出现。
马鲁和克林特正在尝试制造一台能够协助农场工作的实验型机械，而玩家会参与到原型机的完成过程中。
当整段剧情完成后，玩家会获得：
[b]1台完整的机械农场助手。[/b]
同时还会获得：
[b]机械农场助手的制作配方。[/b]
因此，玩家的第一台机器人并不是直接从制作菜单中搓出来的，而是通过剧情真正获得的“原型机”。
之后，如果需要扩大自动化规模，就可以自行制造更多机器人。
[line]
[heading]机器人如何工作[/heading]
机械农场助手会在[b]清晨[/b]开始工作。
每台准备工作的机器人首先会消耗：
[b]1个煤炭。[/b]
成功获得燃料后，机器人就会开始处理自己工作范围内的农田。
目前机器人的主要农业功能包括：
[list]
[*]收获成熟作物；[/*]
[*]耕地；[/*]
[*]施肥；[/*]
[*]播种；[/*]
[*]浇水。[/*]
[/list]也就是说，从土地准备到作物日常维护，再到最后收获，机械农场助手可以承担一套较完整的基础农业工作。
它的目标不是把整个《星露谷物语》全部自动化，而是减少农场发展到中后期之后，大面积种植所带来的重复操作。
[line]
[heading]工作范围[/heading]
每台机械农场助手都围绕自己的[b]机器仓[/b]工作。
机器仓是机器人整个系统的中心。
机器人能够处理：
[b]以机器仓为中心的25格工作范围。[/b]
因此机器仓摆在哪里，会直接决定机器人负责哪一片农田。
玩家可以把机器仓放在某一块主要农田旁边，让机器人负责维护这一片区域。
如果拥有多个机器人，也可以通过多个机器仓分别覆盖不同的农业区域。
这种设计让机器人始终是一件真正存在于农场中的设备，而不是一个无视距离、直接影响整张地图的后台功能。
[line]
[heading]机器仓[/heading]
机械农场助手拥有独立的[b]机器仓[/b]。
机器仓本身也是一个可以正常打开的[b]储物箱[/b]。
玩家可以把物品存放在其中，让机器人的相关物资直接保存在工作区域附近。
因此，机器仓同时承担了几项作用：
它是机械农场助手的基地；
它决定机器人的工作中心；
它提供独立的储物空间；
同时也是整个机器人农业区域的核心设施。
这样的设计可以让机器人真正成为农场布局的一部分，而不是隐藏在后台运行的自动化程序。
[line]
[heading]燃料系统[/heading]
每台机械农场助手在清晨开始工作时都会消耗：
[b]1个煤炭。[/b]
这意味着机器人虽然能够减少大量重复劳动，但依然存在持续的运行成本。
模组没有设计复杂的电池系统、充电槽或者能源数值。
机器人的能源规则保持得非常简单：
[quote]有煤炭，就可以开始工作。[/quote]选择煤炭作为燃料，也是为了让它继续使用星露谷原本已经存在的资源体系，而不需要额外增加一整套新的能源系统。
[line]
[heading]Automate 兼容[/heading]
Mechanical Farmhand 可以与 [b]Automate[/b] 兼容。
如果玩家安装了 Automate，机器仓可以进一步融入原本的自动化系统，让机械农场助手更自然地加入已经高度发展的自动化农场。
但 [b]Automate 并不是必须前置[/b]。
即使完全没有安装 Automate：
机器人的剧情仍然可以正常进行；
机器仓仍然可以正常使用；
机器人仍然能够完成农业工作；
整个模组的主要功能不会受到影响。
所以玩家既可以把它当作一个独立的农业机器人模组，也可以把它作为大型自动化农场中的一个组成部分。
[line]
[heading]游戏进度与平衡[/heading]
Mechanical Farmhand 被有意放在了游戏的中后期。
在真正得到机器人之前，玩家需要经历一段完整的发展过程：
探索矿洞与世界；
收集矮人遗物；
推进博物馆收藏；
捐献足够数量的矿物；
提升与马鲁和克林特的关系；
最终参与农业机器人的开发。
即使获得机器人以后，它仍然需要煤炭作为日常燃料，而且机器仓的位置也会限制它能够负责的农田范围。
因此这个模组并不是想让玩家一开始就跳过种田。
它更像是农场发展过程中自然出现的“下一阶段”。
最开始，玩家自己挥动锄头和水壶。
之后拥有更好的工具。
再之后有洒水器、加工机器和更加完善的农业设施。
而当农场已经发展到一定规模以后，玩家终于能够拥有一台真正帮自己处理农业工作的机械助手。
[line]
[heading]设计理念[/heading]
Mechanical Farmhand 的核心设计理念是：
[quote][b]让自动化本身也成为星露谷故事的一部分。[/b][/quote]机器人的技术不是凭空出现的。
它来源于矮人科技。
它的开发由马鲁和克林特参与。
它的解锁与博物馆收藏有关。
它需要玩家真正推进游戏世界中的关系与探索。
机器人需要燃料。
它需要自己的机器仓。
它只能负责自己附近的农田。
所以最终得到的不是一个隐藏在代码里的“自动种田开关”。
而是一台：
[b]玩家亲自参与开发、真正建造出来、放在农场里，并最终成为农场一部分的机器。[/b]
这也是 [b]Mechanical Farmhand[/b] 最主要的目标。
